verdict: Service in the focus hours is significantly worse than the baseline on late_share.

evidence: [A] 98% of late trains were already late at 34 St-Penn Station (inherited delay). Origins: at or before 168 St: 27, at 145 St: 13, at 59 St-Columbus Circle: 12, at 125 St: 5. Largest time loss on segment 125 St -> 59 St-Columbus Circle (median +65s vs schedule).
[A] 90% of headway gaps at the target already existed at 34 St-Penn Station.

[C] 100% of late trains were already late at 23 St (inherited delay). Origins: at or before 72 St: 18, at or before 50 St: 2, at 59 St-Columbus Circle: 2, at 50 St: 1. Largest time loss on segment 72 St -> 59 St-Columbus Circle (median +80s vs schedule).
[C] 93% of headway gaps at the target already existed at 23 St.

[E] 100% of late trains were already late at 23 St (inherited delay). Origins: at or before 5 Av/53 St: 185, at 50 St: 10, at or before 34 St-Penn Station: 3, at or before 7 Av: 3. Largest time loss on segment 42 St-Port Authority Bus Terminal -> 34 St-Penn Station (median +55s vs schedule).

Weekend problem rate is 1.6x the weekday rate; weekend service changes / planned work likely.
26% of problem arrivals occurred during planned service changes (lift 1.4x).
MTA reports 'Planned ROW Work' as 39% of delays on line(s) A, C, E (1.3x the system share) in the analysed months.
44% of hours with problems ran fewer than 90% of scheduled trains (overall service delivered 83%): cancellations or missing trips are creating gaps.

[A] Time is lost a little at every stop (168 St -> 145 St +30s, 125 St -> 59 St-Columbus Circle +65s, 42 St-Port Authority Bus Terminal -> 34 St-Penn Station +32s): a dwell-time / crowding pattern rather than one bad segment.
[E] Trains that would arrive at 50 St within 180s behind a C/A train lose 116s more there than others (p=0.000; 26% of trips affected); 20% of problem arrivals at the target had such a conflict.
7% of problem arrivals happened while an MTA 'signal' alert was active for the line (problem rate 35% with an alert vs 22% without, lift 1.6x).

recommendations.action: Fill cancelled trips on A, C, E during 00:00-01:00, 01:00-02:00, 06:00-07:00, 09:00-10:00: check crew availability and car assignments
recommendations.rationale: Fewer trains than scheduled are running in the problem hours.
recommendations.expected_effect: Restores scheduled headways; largest APT lever available.

recommendations.action: Dwell-time programme at 14 St and the stops before it during 00:00-01:00, 01:00-02:00, 06:00-07:00, 09:00-10:00: platform controllers, door-closing announcements, step-back crews
recommendations.rationale: Run-time loss is spread across every stop on the approach, the signature of long dwells.
recommendations.expected_effect: Each stop recovers its excess dwell; the effect compounds along the line.

recommendations.action: Review merge priority and dispatch spacing at 50 St, where C, A trains run ahead of E trains bound for 14 St
recommendations.rationale: Arrivals following a train of another route are disproportionately delayed.
recommendations.expected_effect: Fewer merge conflicts; smoother headways for both services.

recommendations.action: Check weekend / late-night planned service changes for A, C, E; use alternates other lines at the station
recommendations.rationale: Planned work is announced in advance.

recommendations.action: Review the general-order (planned work) schedule for A, C, E; add supplement trains or move work windows off 00:00-01:00, 01:00-02:00, 06:00-07:00, 09:00-10:00
recommendations.rationale: Problems coincide with planned service changes.
recommendations.expected_effect: Planned changes stop degrading the analysed hours.

recommendations.action: Check whether scheduled dwell and run times on the approach still match observed loads; re-time the schedule if not
recommendations.rationale: A schedule with unrealistic dwells makes every train late by design.

recommendations.action: Adjust the schedule so C, A and E slots are offset by at least half a headway at 50 St
recommendations.expected_effect: Structural fix that survives day-to-day variability.

sources_used: NY Open Data: trains delayed / incidents
caveats: scheduled counts scaled by observed coverage (1405 polling intervals); hours covered < 50% excluded from service delivered
